---
title: "Recipes"
---

A shared cache does more jobs in a real app than caching. It elects a worker, counts requests, holds sessions and one-time tokens, remembers what was invalidated, and stands in for Redis wherever Redis was only ever there to hold a counter. These are the patterns for those jobs. The examples marked as runnable execute against diskcache-oxide every time these docs are built, so they're known to work.

## Caching

**[Caching expensive calls](caching-expensive-calls.qmd).** The cache-aside pattern, and a small decorator that turns any function into a cached one, with keys built safely from its arguments.

**[Serving stale values while refreshing](stale-while-revalidate.qmd).** Keep a slow page or report available while one worker rebuilds it in the background, or refresh the hot keys ahead of time from a job, so readers never wait and the thundering herd is one worker.

**[Caching responses from other services](caching-http-responses.qmd).** Cache an upstream API's answers, honor its `max-age`, revalidate with ETags, and keep serving the last good answer when it's down.

**[Invalidating groups of keys](invalidating-groups.qmd).** Clear everything cached for one user, one product or one page at once: delete by key prefix, or bump a generation number so stale entries are never read again.

**[Storing your own types](custom-types.qmd).** UUIDs, enums, timedeltas, Paths, dataclasses and Pydantic models in the cache with one registration each, and no pickle.

## Coordinating workers

**[Running a job once across workers](run-once.qmd).** Eight gunicorn workers each schedule the same hourly job, and you want it to run once. `add()` is atomic across processes, so exactly one of them claims it.

**[Rate limiting](rate-limiting.qmd).** Count requests per client in fixed time windows with `add()` and `incr()`, shared by every worker on the machine, with no Redis.

**[Counting things](counters.qmd).** View counts, download totals and usage quotas with `incr()` and `decr()`, flushed to the database with `pop()` so no count is lost or doubled.

**[Single-use keys](single-use-keys.qmd).** Reset links, verification codes and idempotency keys: `pop()` hands a value to exactly one caller, and `add()` accepts a key exactly once.

## State

**[Server-side sessions](sessions.qmd).** Sessions every worker can read, with a sliding idle timeout from `touch()`, an absolute lifetime, and log-out-everywhere by key prefix.

## Deployment and testing

**[Sharing a cache across web workers](web-workers.qmd).** Where to put the cache directory, when to open it with gunicorn, uvicorn, FastAPI, Flask, Django and Celery, how to keep a busy cache from slowing requests, and what to do at shutdown.

**[Using the cache from asyncio](asyncio.qmd).** Read inline, write off the loop, and keep transactions on one thread, in FastAPI, Starlette or aiohttp, until `AsyncCache` lands.

**[Testing code that uses a cache](testing.qmd).** pytest fixtures for a real cache in a temporary directory, a `NullCache` for tests that shouldn't cache at all, and a fake clock for testing expiry without sleeping.

## Coming later

More recipes will arrive with the features they need: `memoize` with stampede protection, tags, cross-process locks and throttles, and `AsyncCache` for asyncio apps. [`FanoutCache`](../user-guide/fanoutcache.qmd) and [`transact()`](../user-guide/transactions.qmd) are here already and have their own guide pages. See the [roadmap](../user-guide/roadmap.qmd).
